Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 49, verses 1–3:

Explanation of the words:

"O you who have believed, do not put forward...": i.e., do not advance ahead in word or deed, for it is from qadama, meaning taqaddama (to go forward).

"before Allah and His Messenger": like one who slaughters on the day of Eid before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ slaughters, and like one of the two shaykhs (Abu Bakr and Umar) wishing to appoint a man over a people before consulting the Messenger ﷺ.

"And fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing": i.e., fear Allah; indeed He hears your words and knows your deeds.

"Do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet": i.e., when you speak, do not speak louder than the Prophet's voice when he speaks.

"And do not speak loudly to him as you speak loudly to one another": i.e., when you confide in him, do not raise your voices in conversation with him as you do among yourselves, out of reverence, honour and esteem for him ﷺ.

"Lest your deeds be nullified": i.e., lest your deeds be made void so that you are not rewarded for them.

"while you perceive not": of their being nullified and voided. For this may be accompanied by contempt for the Prophet ﷺ, especially if it is accompanied by insult and indifference, and that is kufr, we seek refuge in Allah.

"Those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of Allah": i.e., they lower them until it is as if they were whispering to him, and among them was Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him).

"Allah has tested their hearts for piety": i.e., He expanded and widened them to bear the piety of Allah. It is derived from mahana al-adim, when he stretched the hide.

"For them is forgiveness and a great reward": i.e., forgiveness for their sins and a great reward, which is Paradise.

Meaning of the verses:

The words of the Exalted, "O you who have believed": if we seek the connection between this surah and the one before it, it becomes clear if we recall the position of Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) when he wished that no treaty be concluded between the believers and the polytheists, and the position of all the Companions in not exiting the state of ihram and not sacrificing their offerings while the Messenger was commanding them, and they did not respond, until he ﷺ went ahead, sacrificed his offering, and then they sacrificed after him and exited ihram. For those positions we have pointed to contain the meaning of putting forward one's opinion before Allah and His Messenger, and in that is a harm whose extent none knows but Allah. When that state and that difficult circumstance ended, Allah the Exalted revealed His words, "O you who have believed", i.e., in Allah as Lord and God, in Islam as law and religion, and in Muhammad as prophet and messenger. He addressed them by the title of faith to say to them, forbidding: "Do not put forward before Allah and His Messenger", i.e., in speech, in deed, in opinion or in thought. That is, do not say or do anything except in following what Allah and His Messenger have said and legislated. "And fear Allah" in that, for advancing something before Allah and His Messenger have legislated it carries the sense that you are more knowing and wiser than Allah and His Messenger, and this is a great slip whose outcome is evil. Therefore He said, "And fear Allah; indeed Allah is Hearing", i.e., of your words, "Knowing", i.e., of your deeds and conditions. From here, it is obligatory upon the Muslim that he not say, do, judge or issue a ruling by his own opinion except when he knows the word and ruling of Allah and His Messenger, and after he has come to know most of the sayings and rulings of Allah and the Messenger. If he finds nothing of that, he strives (ijtihad) and says or acts according to what he sees as closest to the pleasure of Allah the Exalted. Then if a text from the Book or the Sunnah becomes apparent to him afterwards, he abandons his opinion and speaks according to the Book and the Sunnah.

This is what the first verse indicates. As for the second verse [2], which is His words, "O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet and do not speak loudly to him as you speak loudly to one another, lest your deeds be nullified while you perceive not", it obliges the Muslim to good manners with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. First, He forbade them, may Allah be pleased with them, from raising their voices above the voice of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when they speak with him, and obligated them to honour, glorify and revere the Prophet, such that the voice of any one of them when speaking with the Messenger of Allah is lower than the voice of the Messenger ﷺ. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), when he spoke to the Messenger of Allah, would speak to him in a low, confidential tone. Second, He forbade them, when they confided in the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, from speaking loudly to him as some of them spoke loudly to others, but rather it is obligatory for them to revere and glorify him. He informed them that He fears for them, if they do not revere the Messenger of Allah and do not honour him, that their deeds will be nullified as they are nullified by shirk and kufr, while they perceive not. For raising the voice to the Messenger, and calling him with a loud voice, "O Muhammad" or "O Prophet of Allah" or "O Messenger of Allah", and with loud voices, if accompanied by contempt, insult or indifference, becomes kufr that definitely nullifies the deed. In the third verse [3], Allah the Exalted praises people who lower their voices, i.e., reduce them, in the presence of the Messenger of Allah, i.e., in his presence and before him, such as Abu Bakr and Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both). About these He informs that He tested their hearts for piety, i.e., He widened and expanded them to bear the piety of Allah and His Messenger ﷺ. He said, "Piety is here," pointing to his chest three times. And He gives them glad tidings, the best of tidings: that for them from Him is forgiveness for their sins, and a great reward on the day they meet Him, which is Paradise, the abode of the pious. May Allah make us among them by His grace and mercy.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1. It is not permissible for a Muslim to put his opinion or ijtihad (independent reasoning) ahead of the Book and the Sunnah. There is no opinion or ijtihad except where there is no text from the Book or the Sunnah. He must, when he exercises ijtihad, ensure that what he reaches is closest to the intent of Allah and His Messenger, i.e., most adherent to the Shari'ah. If a text from the Book or the Sunnah becomes apparent to him after ijtihad, he returns to the Book and the Sunnah and leaves his opinion or ijtihad immediately and without hesitation.

2. Since Allah has taken His Prophet to Himself and no Messenger of Allah remains among us to speak with or confide in, whereby we lower our voices, it is incumbent upon us, when the Messenger of Allah is mentioned among us or his hadith is mentioned, to show good manners: we do not laugh, we do not raise our voices, and we do not show any contempt or indifference, lest our deeds be nullified while we perceive not.

3. Those who frequent the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ must not raise their voices in it except for the necessity of a lesson, a sermon, the call to prayer, or the iqamah.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 49, verses 4–8:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Indeed, those who call out to you from behind the chambers⦾﴾: i.e., the chambers of his wives. Those who called out to him were a delegation of the Bedouin Arabs of Banu Tamim, among them al-Zibriqan ibn Badr, al-Aqra' ibn Habis and Uyayna ibn Hisn.

﴿Most of them do not use their reason⦾﴾: i.e., in what they did regarding your lofty station and your exalted, noble position.

﴿And if they had been patient until you came out to them⦾﴾: i.e., if they had waited for you until you came out after rising from your midday rest.

﴿It would have been better for them⦾﴾: i.e., than that calling out in loud voices from every door of the chambers.

﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful⦾﴾: i.e., Forgiving toward those among them who repent, and Merciful toward them, since they did wrong twice: the first by raising their voices, and the second by calling out to him and saying, "Come out to us, for our praise is an adornment and our blame is a disgrace."

﴿A corrupt person brings news⦾﴾: i.e., one who is given to wickedness, who commits one of the major sins; and "news" means important information.

﴿Then verify⦾﴾: i.e., establish the truth before you speak, act or judge.

﴿Lest you harm a people in ignorance⦾﴾: i.e., for fear that you might harm a people through ignorance on your part.

﴿And then become regretful for what you have done⦾﴾: i.e., that you become regretful for your mistaken deed.

﴿And know that among you is the Messenger of Allah⦾﴾: i.e., beware of lying or speaking falsehood, for revelation descends and your lies and falsehood will be exposed.

﴿If he obeyed you in much of the matter, you would be in difficulty⦾﴾: i.e., you would fall into severe hardship and, at times, into sin.

﴿But Allah has made faith beloved to you and has made it pleasing in your hearts, and has made disbelief, defiance and disobedience hateful to you⦾﴾: i.e., He made hatred of disbelief, defiance such as lying, and disobedience by abandoning an obligation or committing a forbidden act, beloved to your hearts.

﴿Those are the rightly guided⦾﴾: i.e., those upon whom was done what was done, namely the making faith beloved and disbelief hateful, and what is mentioned with it. They are the rightly guided, i.e., those who travel the path of right guidance.

﴿As a bounty from Allah and favor⦾﴾: i.e., He favored them with a bounty and bestowed a blessing upon them.

﴿And Allah is Knowing and Wise⦾﴾: i.e., Knowing of His creation and what they do, Wise in His management of His servants, this in general and in particular; Knowing of those rightly guided ones, Wise in His bestowing favor upon them.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to discipline the believers in their conduct toward their Prophet ﷺ. Allah the Exalted censured people who showed coarseness and harshness. It is said that they were a delegation of the Bedouin Arabs of Banu Tamim, among them al-Zibriqan ibn Badr, al-Aqra' ibn Habis and Uyayna ibn Hisn. They came while the Messenger was resting at midday, stood at the doors of the chambers and called out in the loudest voices, "O Muhammad! O Muhammad! (ﷺ) Come out to us, for our praise is an adornment and our blame is a disgrace." So Allah revealed this noble verse about them as a discipline: ﴿Indeed, those who call out to you from behind the chambers⦾﴾ — the chambers of the wives of the Messenger ﷺ, and the doors of the chambers faced the mosque. ﴿Most of them do not use their reason⦾﴾, i.e., in what they did regarding the noble station and lofty rank of the Messenger. ﴿And if they had been patient until you came out to them⦾﴾, after your rising from your midday rest, ﴿it would have been better for them⦾﴾, i.e., than that calling with raised voices from behind the chambers. His saying, ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful⦾﴾, means: Forgiving toward those who repent among them, and Merciful toward them, since He did not hasten their punishment, opened for them the door of repentance, disciplined them, and did not rebuke or act harshly.

As for His saying in the third verse of this context [6]: ﴿O you who have believed, if a corrupt person comes to you with information, then verify it, lest you harm a people in ignorance and then become regretful for what you have done⦾﴾. Although this verse has a cause of revelation, namely that the Prophet ﷺ sent al-Walid ibn Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt to the Banu al-Mustaliq to collect the zakat of their wealth. There had been enmity between them and al-Walid's family in the pre-Islamic period, so al-Walid recalled this and feared to enter their homes. This was from the whisperings of Satan. He returned and concealed the fear that had afflicted him, reporting that they had refused to give him the zakat and had intended to kill him, so he fled from them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ became angry and resolved to fight them.

He remained in this state until a delegation of them came seeking to appease the Messenger of Allah and to make amends with him, fearing that some ill report about them had reached him. They informed him that they were upon the covenant and that al-Walid had turned back on the road and had not reached them. The Messenger sent Khalid ibn al-Walid by another route, and he reached them before sunset, and behold, they were calling the adhan and praying Maghrib and 'Isha'. He knew that they had not apostatized and that they were upon good, praise be to Allah. He brought the zakat, and Allah revealed this verse. I say: although this verse was revealed concerning a specific cause, it is general and a fundamental and important principle. Individuals, communities and states must not accept reports conveyed to them, nor act upon their requirements, except after verification and proper clarification, out of dislike of harming an individual or a group without justification, and without a reason other than evil and slander which its bearer may intend for his own benefit, by bringing about a gain or averting a harm from himself. Therefore, adopting the principle of verification and clarification when hearing a report from a person not known for piety, uprightness and complete trustworthiness is obligatory, to safeguard the dignity of individuals and protect their lives and property. Praise be to Allah for a just and merciful law such as this. As for His saying ﴿If a corrupt person comes to you⦾﴾, the "corrupt person" means one who commits a major sin, such as lying for example; "news" means an important report; "verification" means establishing the truth; and His saying ﴿lest you harm a people⦾﴾ means lest you harm them in their bodies and property through your lack of knowledge, which is the ignorance; and His saying ﴿and then become regretful for what you have done⦾﴾ means as a consequence of the mistaken measure you have taken.

As for His saying in the verse [7]: ﴿And know⦾﴾, the Lord the Exalted draws the attention of the Muslims to a reality they are heedless of, namely the presence of the Messenger ﷺ living among them, to whom revelation descends. This is a state that requires them to maintain truthfulness in word and deed, otherwise revelation will immediately expose them if they lie in speech or action, as it exposed al-Walid when he reported what was not true. This is the first point. Second, if the Messenger ﷺ were to obey them in everything they see and propose, they would fall into problems that expose them to unbearable hardships, and even into grave sins. This is the meaning of His saying ﴿And know that among you is the Messenger of Allah. If he obeyed you in much of the matter, you would be in difficulty⦾﴾, and His saying ﴿But Allah has made faith beloved to you and made it pleasing in your hearts, and has made disbelief, defiance and disobedience hateful to you⦾﴾. He thereby protected you from much of lying against your Messenger, proposing things to him, or imposing your opinions. His saying ﴿Those are the rightly guided⦾﴾ means: those, the companions of the Messenger of Allah, are those who travel the path of right guidance, so they do not go astray or stray. His saying ﴿As a bounty from Allah and favor⦾﴾ means: their guidance was a bounty from Allah and a favor. Allah is Knowing of them, their intentions and the motives of their souls, and Wise in His management; He qualified the companions of the Messenger of Allah for goodness and bestowed it upon them, so they are the best of this Ummah without exception, and no one who comes after them has any hope of surpassing them in virtue and perfection, in this world or the next. May Allah be pleased with them and make them pleased, all of them, and may He include us with them. Amin.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Demonstration of the exalted station of Muhammad ﷺ and the nobility of his rank.

2- The obligation to verify reports of importance which may result in harm or injury to the person about whom they are spoken, and the prohibition of haste that leads to acting on suspicion, whereby the doer will later regret it in this world and the next.

3- Among the greatest blessings upon the believer is that Allah makes faith beloved to him and adorns it in his heart, and makes disbelief, defiance and disobedience hateful to him; by this the believer becomes the most rightly guided of creation after the companions of the Messenger ﷺ.

Explanation of the words:

﴿And if they had been patient until you came out to them⦾﴾: i.e., if they had waited for you until you came out after rising from your midday rest.

﴿It would have been better for them⦾﴾: i.e., than that calling out in loud voices from every door of the chambers.

﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful⦾﴾: i.e., Forgiving toward those among them who repent, and Merciful toward them, since they did wrong twice: the first by raising their voices, and the second by calling out to him and saying, "Come out to us, for our praise is an adornment and our blame is a disgrace."

﴿Then verify⦾﴾: i.e., establish the truth before you speak, act or judge.

﴿Lest you harm a people in ignorance⦾﴾: i.e., for fear that you might harm a people through ignorance on your part.

﴿And know that among you is the Messenger of Allah⦾﴾: i.e., beware of lying or speaking falsehood, for revelation descends and your lies and falsehood will be exposed.

﴿If he obeyed you in much of the matter, you would be in difficulty⦾﴾: i.e., you would fall into severe hardship and, at times, into sin.

﴿As a bounty from Allah and favor⦾﴾: i.e., He favored them with a bounty and bestowed a blessing upon them.

﴿And Allah is Knowing and Wise⦾﴾: i.e., Knowing of His creation and what they do, Wise in His management of His servants, this in general and in particular; Knowing of those rightly guided ones, Wise in His bestowing favor upon them.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to discipline the believers in their conduct toward their Prophet ﷺ. Allah the Exalted censured people who showed coarseness and harshness. It is said that they were a delegation of the Bedouin Arabs of Banu Tamim, among them al-Zibriqan ibn Badr, al-Aqra' ibn Habis and Uyayna ibn Hisn. They came while the Messenger was resting at midday, stood at the doors of the chambers and called out in the loudest voices, "O Muhammad! O Muhammad! (ﷺ) Come out to us, for our praise is an adornment and our blame is a disgrace." So Allah revealed this noble verse about them as a discipline: ﴿Indeed, those who call out to you from behind the chambers⦾﴾ — the chambers of the wives of the Messenger ﷺ, and the doors of the chambers faced the mosque. ﴿Most of them do not use their reason⦾﴾, i.e., in what they did regarding the noble station and lofty rank of the Messenger. ﴿And if they had been patient until you came out to them⦾﴾, after your rising from your midday rest, ﴿it would have been better for them⦾﴾, i.e., than that calling with raised voices from behind the chambers. Although this verse has a cause of revelation, namely that the Prophet ﷺ sent al-Walid ibn Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt to the Banu al-Mustaliq to collect the zakat of their wealth. There had been enmity between them and al-Walid's family in the pre-Islamic period, so al-Walid recalled this and feared to enter their homes. This was from the whisperings of Satan. He returned and concealed the fear that had afflicted him, reporting that they had refused to give him the zakat and had intended to kill him, so he fled from them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ became angry and resolved to fight them.

He remained in this state until a delegation of them came seeking to appease the Messenger of Allah and to make amends with him, fearing that some ill report about them had reached him. They informed him that they were upon the covenant and that al-Walid had turned back on the road and had not reached them. The Messenger sent Khalid ibn al-Walid by another route, and he reached them before sunset, and behold, they were calling the adhan and praying Maghrib and 'Isha'. He knew that they had not apostatized and that they were upon good, praise be to Allah. He brought the zakat, and Allah revealed this verse. I say: although this verse was revealed concerning a specific cause, it is general and a fundamental and important principle. Individuals, communities and states must not accept reports conveyed to them, nor act upon their requirements, except after verification and proper clarification, out of dislike of harming an individual or a group without justification, and without a reason other than evil and slander which its bearer may intend for his own benefit, by bringing about a gain or averting a harm from himself. Therefore, adopting the principle of verification and clarification when hearing a report from a person not known for piety, uprightness and complete trustworthiness is obligatory, to safeguard the dignity of individuals and protect their lives and property. As for His saying in the verse [7]: ﴿And know⦾﴾, the Lord the Exalted draws the attention of the Muslims to a reality they are heedless of, namely the presence of the Messenger ﷺ living among them, to whom revelation descends. This is a state that requires them to maintain truthfulness in word and deed, otherwise revelation will immediately expose them if they lie in speech or action, as it exposed al-Walid when he reported what was not true. This is the first point. Second, if the Messenger ﷺ were to obey them in everything they see and propose, they would fall into problems that expose them to unbearable hardships, and even into grave sins. This is the meaning of His saying ﴿And know that among you is the Messenger of Allah. If he obeyed you in much of the matter, you would be in difficulty⦾﴾, and His saying ﴿But Allah has made faith beloved to you and made it pleasing in your hearts, and has made disbelief, defiance and disobedience hateful to you⦾﴾. He thereby protected you from much of lying against your Messenger, proposing things to him, or imposing your opinions. His saying ﴿Those are the rightly guided⦾﴾ means: those, the companions of the Messenger of Allah, are those who travel the path of right guidance, so they do not go astray or stray. His saying ﴿As a bounty from Allah and favor⦾﴾ means: their guidance was a bounty from Allah and a favor. Allah is Knowing of them, their intentions and the motives of their souls, and Wise in His management; He qualified the companions of the Messenger of Allah for goodness and bestowed it upon them, so they are the best of this Ummah without exception, and no one who comes after them has any hope of surpassing them in virtue and perfection, in this world or the next. May Allah be pleased with them and make them pleased, all of them, and may He include us with them. Amin.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to discipline the believers in their conduct toward their Prophet ﷺ. Allah the Exalted censured people who showed coarseness and harshness. It is said that they were a delegation of the Bedouin Arabs of Banu Tamim, among them al-Zibriqan ibn Badr, al-Aqra' ibn Habis and Uyayna ibn Hisn. They came while the Messenger was resting at midday, stood at the doors of the chambers and called out in the loudest voices, "O Muhammad! O Muhammad! (ﷺ) Come out to us, for our praise is an adornment and our blame is a disgrace." This is the meaning of His saying ﴿And know that among you is the Messenger of Allah. May Allah be pleased with them and make them pleased, all of them, and may He include us with them. Amin.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 49, verses 9–13:

Explanation of the words:

"And if two groups of the believers fight, then make peace between them": i.e., two groups, whether small or large in number, from among the Muslims.

"Then make peace between them": i.e., they intended to fight or actually engaged in fighting, so make peace between them by repairing what has been corrupted between them.

"But if one of them transgresses against the other": i.e., it oversteps after the reconciliation, by rejecting that and not being content with the judgment of Allah.

"Then fight the one that transgresses until it returns to the command of Allah": i.e., fight, O believers, united against the group that transgressed, until it returns to the truth.

"And if it returns, then make peace between them with justice": i.e., it has returned to the truth after being fought, so make peace between them with justice, that is, with truth.

"And act justly. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly": i.e., and be just in your judgment, for Allah loves those who are people of justice.

"The believers are but brothers": i.e., in the Islamic religion.

"So make peace between your two brothers": i.e., if they dispute something and quarrel over it.

"And fear Allah that you may receive mercy": i.e., fear His punishment, hoping that you will be shown mercy if you fear Him.

"Let not a people ridicule [another] people": i.e., let no group among you belittle and scorn other people.

"Perhaps they may be better than them": i.e., in the sight of Allah Most High; what matters is what is with Allah, not what is with people.

"Nor defame one another": i.e., do not find fault with one another, for you are like a single person.

"Nor insult one another by [offensive] nicknames": i.e., let no one call another by a title he dislikes, such as "O sinner" or "O ignoramus."

"How evil is the name of disobedience after faith": i.e., how ugly is the name of wickedness that a person acquires after his faith and Islam.

"And whoever does not repent, then it is those who are the wrongdoers": i.e., whoever defames and insults the believers, those are the far-removed wrongdoers.

"Avoid much of [what may be] suspicion": i.e., accusations for which there are no causes or indications that necessitate them.

"Indeed, some suspicion is sin": i.e., such as thinking ill of the people of goodness among the believers.

"And do not spy, and do not backbite one another": i.e., do not pursue the faults of the Muslims or search them out.

"Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his brother when he is dead?": i.e., it is not fitting for anyone to like to eat the flesh of his dead brother, nor of him while alive.

"So you would detest it": i.e., this was presented to you first, and you detested it; so likewise detest it while he is alive, which is backbiting, just as you detested eating his flesh when dead.

"And We made you peoples and tribes": i.e., plural of "shu'ub," and the tribe is smaller than the shu'ub.

"That you may know one another": i.e., so that some of you may know others, so get to know one another, not for boasting of the nobility of lineages.

"Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you": i.e., the one among you who is most strongly devoted to Allah by carrying out His commands and abstaining from His prohibitions is the most noble in the sight of Allah.

"Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted": i.e., He knows you and your circumstances, and is aware of what you are upon of perfection and deficiency; nothing of the affairs of the servants is hidden from Him.

Meaning of the verses:

His saying, may He be exalted, "And if two groups of the believers fight..." The noble context continues in seeking to discipline and train the Muslims and prepare them for worldly and otherworldly perfection. In verses [9] and [10] of this context, Allah Most High guides the Muslims to the way of treating the problem of armed conflict among Muslims, which may occur in the Islamic society from time to time due to human weakness, and which is almost one of the necessities of human life, its causes being many and needing no mention. So He, may He be exalted, said, "And if two groups" i.e., two bodies "of the believers fight," even if that is between only two persons, "then make peace" O Muslims "between them" by eliminating the causes of disagreement and satisfying both parties with what is right and good. This is not difficult where there are believing hearts and divine guidance. His saying, "But if one of them transgresses" i.e., one of the two groups oversteps after the reconciliation "against the other," by rejecting the judgment of Allah on the basis of which the reconciliation was made, "then fight" united "the one that transgresses" i.e., oversteps "until it returns to the command of Allah" i.e., to the truth. "And if it returns" i.e., submits to the truth and accepts it, "then make peace between them with justice, and act justly" in your judgment always and forever. "Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly." His saying, may He be exalted, in verse [10], "The believers are but brothers, so make peace between your two brothers and fear Allah that you may receive mercy," affirms Islamic brotherhood and restricts the believers to it exclusively: the believers are only brothers to one another, and therefore it is obligatory to mend every breach and reform every corruption that appears among them, and not to be lax about that. "And fear Allah" in that, so do not be negligent or lax until believing blood is shed and the structure of faith and Islam is shattered in its lands. His saying, "that you may receive mercy," so that your structure is not shattered, your nation is not scattered, and it does not become groups and factions hostile to one another, killing one another.

Since the believers did not fear Allah in promptly reconciling the disputing Islamic factions, there resulted corruption and evil whose extent is known only to Allah, in the Islamic West and East. His saying in verse [11], "O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [another] people, perhaps they may be better than them, nor women [ridicule] other women, perhaps they may be better than them," since among the factors of conflict and fighting and their causes is a believer's mockery of his brother and his contempt for him because of his poor condition, shabby clothing, and lack of means. By this verse, Allah Most High forbids a Muslim to despise his Muslim brother and belittle him, warning that the one who is despised and mocked may often be better in the sight of Allah than the one who despises him. What matters is what is with Allah, not what is with people. Men and women are equal in this, so it is not lawful for a believing woman to belittle and despise her believing sister, perhaps she may be better than her in rank with Allah. What matters is rank with Allah, not with people. Just as He forbade mocking believing men and women because it leads to enmity, hatred, and then fighting, He likewise forbade defaming and insulting with nicknames. He, may He be exalted, said, "And do not defame one another or insult one another by [offensive] nicknames. How evil is the name of disobedience after faith." The meaning of "do not defame yourselves" is: do not blame one another for any fault, for you are like one person; whoever blames his Muslim brother has, as it were, blamed himself, just as the one blamed may return the fault with a fault of the one who blamed him. This is the meaning of "nor defame yourselves." His saying, "nor insult one another by nicknames," means a Muslim should not call his brother by a title he dislikes, for that leads to enmity and fighting. His saying, "How evil is the name of disobedience after faith," means: it is most extremely evil for a Muslim to be called by the title of wickedness after he has become a believer, upright and complete in his character and manners. It is not lawful for a believer to say to his brother, "O wicked one," or "O unbeliever," or "O fornicator," or "O corrupt one," for how evil is the name of wickedness. Whoever calls a Muslim by evil titles is considered a wicked person, and how evil is the name of wickedness for him to be wicked after his faith in Allah, His meeting, and His Messenger and what he brought. His saying, may He be exalted, "And whoever does not repent" i.e., from belittling and despising the Muslims and calling them by titles they dislike, "then it is those who are the wrongdoers," who expose themselves to the anger and punishment of Allah.

His saying in verse [12], "O you who have believed, avoid much of [what may be] suspicion. Indeed, some suspicion is sin, and do not spy, and do not backbite one another," Allah Most High addresses the Muslims by the title of faith, for by it they have become living, hearing, seeing, and able to act and refrain, since faith is like the spirit: when it enters the body, it moves, so the eye sees, the ear hears, the tongue speaks, and the heart understands.

He says, "O you who have believed, avoid much of suspicion," which is every suspicion that lacks what necessitates it of indications, circumstances, and attending conditions. He gives the reason for this prohibition, which implies prohibition, saying, "Indeed, some suspicion is sin," such as thinking ill of the people of goodness and righteousness in the community, for thinking ill of them may lead to false speech, evil action, or the neglect of good, and so it is a great sin. His saying, "And do not spy," means do not pursue the Muslims' faults and defects by searching for them and looking into them, because of the great harm in that. His saying, "and do not backbite one another," means that none of you should mention his brother in his absence in a way he dislikes. Here, among the sound hadiths, it is related in meaning that "a man asked the Messenger ﷺ about backbiting, and he said: 'Your mentioning your brother in a way he dislikes.' The man said: 'But if what I say is in him?' He said: 'If what is in him is what you say, you have backbited him; and if it is not in him, you have slandered him, and slander is worse than backbiting.'" His saying, "Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his brother when he is dead?" The answer is definitely no. So just as the flesh of your brother was presented to you dead and you detested it, then detest likewise eating his flesh alive, which is his honor, and honor is more precious and dearer than the body. His saying, "And fear Allah," regarding the backbiting of one another, for backbiting is among the causes of ruin and corruption among the Muslims. His saying, "Indeed, Allah is Accepting of repentance and Merciful," is a clause giving the reason for the command to repent: He, may He be exalted, informs that He accepts the repentance of those who repent and that He is merciful to the believers, and among the manifestations of that is that He forbade backbiting the believer because of the harm and injury it causes him.

His saying, may He be exalted, in verse [13], "O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another." This is a call which is the last of Allah's calls to His servants in this surah, and it is more general than the call by the title of faith. He said, "O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female," from Adam and Eve as to origin, just as every human being is created from two parents, one male and the other female. "And We made you peoples and tribes," and clans, branches, and sub-divisions. All of this is for the wisdom of mutual knowledge. He did not make you like the kind of animals that do not know other animals, but made you peoples, tribes, extended families, and households for the wisdom of mutual knowledge, which requires cooperation, since cooperation among individuals is necessary for the establishment of a good and prosperous society. So know one another and cooperate, and do not separate for the sake of boasting of lineages, for there is no worth in ancestry or lineage when a person is base in his self and character and corrupt in his conduct. "Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you." Honor and perfection lie in what a person possesses of purification of soul, soundness of character, correctness of judgment, and abundance of knowledge.

His saying, may He be exalted, "Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted," is a clause giving the reason, in which He, may He be exalted, explains that He is knowing of people, knowing of their outward and inward states, and of what perfects and makes them happy, and Acquainted with everything in their lives. So let legislation be submitted to Him in permitting and forbidding, commanding and prohibiting, for He has knowledge of the present state and the outcome, and of what makes a person happy and what makes him wretched. So believe in Him and obey Him, and you will be perfected and made happy.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The obligation on the Muslims to hasten to reconcile between them whenever corruption or disorder occurs among them.

2- The obligation of the Muslims to cooperate in disciplining any group that transgresses and oversteps until it returns to the truth.

3- The obligation to judge with justice in any matter concerning the Muslims and others.

4- Affirmation of Islamic brotherhood and the obligation to realize it in word and deed.

5- The prohibition of mockery, defaming, and insulting with nicknames among the Muslims.

6- The obligation to avoid every suspicion for which there is no strong indication or circumstance calling for it.

7- The prohibition of espionage, i.e., pursuing the Muslims' faults, exposing them, and informing people of them.

8- The prohibition of backbiting and tale-bearing (namimah). Tale-bearing is conveying speech in a manner intended to cause corruption. Therefore, it is permissible to mention a person in his absence in certain contexts: complaining of injustice, by mentioning whoever wronged one so as to remove the injustice; seeking help in changing an evil by mentioning the one committing it; seeking a legal opinion, as when the questioner says, "So-and-so wronged me with such-and-such, is that permissible for him?"; warning Muslims against evil by mentioning its doer, intending that they be wary of him; one who openly commits wickedness has no protected reputation (lit. no backbiting); and identifying someone by a nickname by which he is known and by which no one knows him otherwise.

9- The prohibition of boasting of lineages and the obligation of mutual knowledge for the sake of cooperation.

10- There is no nobility or honor except the nobility and honor of piety: "Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you." In the hadith: "There is no superiority of an Arab over a non-Arab, nor of a white over a black, except by piety," related by al-Tabarani.

Explanation of the words:

"And if two groups of the believers fight, then make peace between them": i.e., two groups, whether small or large in number, from among the Muslims.

"Then make peace between them": i.e., they intended to fight or actually engaged in fighting, so make peace between them by repairing what has been corrupted between them.

"But if one of them transgresses against the other": i.e., it oversteps after the reconciliation, by rejecting that and not being content with the judgment of Allah.

"Then fight the one that transgresses until it returns to the command of Allah": i.e., fight, O believers, united against the group that transgressed, until it returns to the truth.

"And if it returns, then make peace between them with justice": i.e., it has returned to the truth after being fought, so make peace between them with justice, that is, with truth.

"And act justly. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly": i.e., and be just in your judgment, for Allah loves those who are people of justice.

"The believers are but brothers": i.e., in the Islamic religion.

"So make peace between your two brothers": i.e., if they dispute something and quarrel over it.

"And fear Allah that you may receive mercy": i.e., fear His punishment, hoping that you will be shown mercy if you fear Him.

"Let not a people ridicule [another] people": i.e., let no group among you belittle and scorn other people.

"Perhaps they may be better than them": i.e., in the sight of Allah Most High; what matters is what is with Allah, not what is with people.

"Nor defame one another": i.e., do not find fault with one another, for you are like a single person.

"Nor insult one another by [offensive] nicknames": i.e., let no one call another by a title he dislikes, such as "O sinner" or "O ignoramus."

"How evil is the name of disobedience after faith": i.e., how ugly is the name of wickedness that a person acquires after his faith and Islam.

"And whoever does not repent, then it is those who are the wrongdoers": i.e., whoever defames and insults the believers, those are the far-removed wrongdoers.

"Avoid much of [what may be] suspicion": i.e., accusations for which there are no causes or indications that necessitate them.

"Indeed, some suspicion is sin": i.e., such as thinking ill of the people of goodness among the believers.

"And do not spy, and do not backbite one another": i.e., do not pursue the faults of the Muslims or search them out.

"Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his brother when he is dead?": i.e., it is not fitting for anyone to like to eat the flesh of his dead brother, nor of him while alive.

"So you would detest it": i.e., this was presented to you first, and you detested it; so likewise detest it while he is alive, which is backbiting, just as you detested eating his flesh when dead.

"And We made you peoples and tribes": i.e., plural of "shu'ub," and the tribe is smaller than the shu'ub.

"That you may know one another": i.e., so that some of you may know others, so get to know one another, not for boasting of the nobility of lineages.

"Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you": i.e., the one among you who is most strongly devoted to Allah by carrying out His commands and abstaining from His prohibitions is the most noble in the sight of Allah.

"Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted": i.e., He knows you and your circumstances, and is aware of what you are upon of perfection and deficiency; nothing of the affairs of the servants is hidden from Him.

His saying, may He be exalted, "And if two groups of the believers fight..." The noble context continues in seeking to discipline and train the Muslims and prepare them for worldly and otherworldly perfection. What matters is what is with Allah, not what is with people. Men and women are equal in this, so it is not lawful for a believing woman to belittle and despise her believing sister, perhaps she may be better than her in rank with Allah. What matters is rank with Allah, not with people. He, may He be exalted, said, "And do not defame one another or insult one another by [offensive] nicknames. How evil is the name of disobedience after faith." His saying, "nor insult one another by nicknames," means a Muslim should not call his brother by a title he dislikes, for that leads to enmity and fighting. His saying, "How evil is the name of disobedience after faith," means: it is most extremely evil for a Muslim to be called by the title of wickedness after he has become a believer, upright and complete in his character and manners. His saying, "and do not backbite one another," means that none of you should mention his brother in his absence in a way he dislikes. His saying, "And fear Allah," regarding the backbiting of one another, for backbiting is among the causes of ruin and corruption among the Muslims. This is a call which is the last of Allah's calls to His servants in this surah, and it is more general than the call by the title of faith. He said, "O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female," from Adam and Eve as to origin, just as every human being is created from two parents, one male and the other female. "And We made you peoples and tribes," and clans, branches, and sub-divisions. All of this is for the wisdom of mutual knowledge. He did not make you like the kind of animals that do not know other animals, but made you peoples, tribes, extended families, and households for the wisdom of mutual knowledge, which requires cooperation, since cooperation among individuals is necessary for the establishment of a good and prosperous society. Honor and perfection lie in what a person possesses of purification of soul, soundness of character, correctness of judgment, and abundance of knowledge.

The Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 49, verses 14–18:

Explanation of the words:

"The Bedouins say: We have believed." They are a group of the Bedouins of the Banu Asad who came to the Messenger and said to him, "We have believed," while they were not believers.

"Say: You have not believed, but say: We have submitted (aslamna)." That is: say to them, "You have not yet believed, but say 'We have submitted' (aslamna), meaning we have surrendered and complied."

"And faith has not yet entered your hearts." That is: faith has not yet entered your hearts, but it is expected that it will enter.

"And if you obey Allah and His Messenger." That is: in faith, in performing the obligatory duties, and in avoiding what is forbidden.

"He will not deprive you of anything of your deeds." That is: He will not reduce anything from the reward of your deeds.

"Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful." That is: Forgiving toward the believers and Merciful to them if they are sincere in their faith.

"The believers are only..." That is: truly and genuinely, not by claim and utterance, they are.

"Those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger." That is: in Allah as Lord and God, and in the Messenger Muhammad as prophet and messenger.

"Then they have not doubted." That is: they have not harbored doubt about what they believed in.

"And have striven with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah." That is: they strove alongside the Messenger of Allah against the enemies of Allah, who are the disbelievers, with their wealth and their lives.

"Those are the truthful." That is: in their faith, not those who said "We have believed" with their tongues and submitted outwardly without submitting inwardly.

"Say: Will you inform Allah of your religion?" That is: say to them, O our Messenger, to these Bedouins: Will you inform Allah of your religion?

"They consider it a favor to you that they have embraced Islam." That is: their having embraced Islam without fighting, while others embraced it after fighting.

"Say: Do not consider your Islam a favor to me." That is: you have no right to that; rather the right belongs to Allah, who guided you to faith, if you are truthful in your claim that you are believers.

"Indeed, Allah knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth." That is: Allah knows what is hidden in the heavens and what is hidden in the earth, so the matter of one who is sincere in his faith and the matter of one who lies is not concealed from Him, nor is the matter of one who embraced Islam out of desire or out of fear.

Meaning of the verses:

The Most High said, "The Bedouins say, 'We have believed'" (49:14). These were a group of the Bedouins of the Banu Asad who came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Madinah with their children and women in a year of drought, and they outwardly showed Islam while not being believers in their hearts. They would come to the Messenger ﷺ and go back, saying: "The Arabs have come to you on the backs of their mounts, and we have come to you with our children, dependents and offspring, and we did not fight you as such-and-such and such-and-such fought you." They would thus confer a favor upon the Messenger of Allah, while they wanted charity and would say, "Give us." So Allah revealed this verse as an education and instruction for them, completing what Surah al-Hujurat contains of the types of guidance and Islamic upbringing. He said, "The Bedouins say," the Bedouins of the Banu Asad, "We have believed," meaning: we have affirmed the oneness of Allah and your prophethood. "Say [to them] in response to them: You have not yet believed, but rather the correct course is that you say, 'We have submitted,'" meaning: we have yielded to Islam and complied to accept it, which is outward Islam. "And faith has not yet entered your hearts, but it will enter, if Allah wills." "And if you obey Allah and His Messenger, O Bedouins, in true faith and in all other duties, He will not deprive you, that is, Allah will not reduce from the rewards of your righteous deeds that you perform in obedience to Allah and His Messenger anything, even if it be little."

His saying, "Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful," in this sentence is an encouragement for them toward sincere faith and correct submission. He informed them that Allah is Forgiving to those who repent and Merciful to them and to the believers, so repent to Him and be truthful with Him, and He will forgive you and have mercy upon you. His saying in verse [15], "The believers are only..." to the end of the verse, describes them by true faith, as a call from Him to them, that perhaps they may believe. He said, "The believers are only," that is, truly and genuinely, "those who have believed in Allah as Lord and God, and in His Messenger as a prophet to be obeyed. Then they have not doubted," meaning they never doubted the validity of what they believed in. "And have striven," that is, against themselves, binding themselves to readiness to undertake the legal duties in ease and in hardship, as they strove with their wealth and their lives against the enemies of Islam from among the polytheists and disbelievers. That striving with life and wealth has no aim except seeking the pleasure of Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, that is, it was not for any worldly material purpose but for the pleasure of Allah and the elevation of the word of Allah. "Those are the truthful in the claim of faith." His saying in verse [16], "Say: Will you inform Allah of your religion?" That is: say, O our Messenger, to those Bedouins who said "We have believed" while faith had not entered their hearts: Will you inform Allah of your religion, that is, of your faith and obedience, and make Him aware of them, while Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, and Allah is Knowing of all things? There is no sense in your informing Allah of your religion when He knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth and He is Knowing of all things. It is a manifestation of your ignorance of Allah, the Most High, for if you knew that He knows what is in the heavens and in the earth, both minute and great, you would not have made the claims you made about informing Allah of your faith and obedience to Him. His saying in verse [17], "They consider it a favor to you that they have embraced Islam," that is: those Bedouins confer a favor upon you, O our Messenger, by their faith, since they said, "We have believed in you," and did not fight you as others did. Say to them, "Do not consider your Islam a favor to me," and turn away from this and say to them: rather, Allah confers a favor upon you that He guided you to faith, if you are truthful in your claim of faith. So the favor is Allah's upon you, not that you confer a favor upon His Messenger. His saying, "Indeed, Allah knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth," that is: whatever is hidden in the heavens and whatever is hidden in the earth, from a bird flying in the sky, a swimmer in the water, and a grazer in the dry land, He does not need you to inform Him of your religion or to confer favors on His Messenger ﷺ. "And Allah is Seeing of what you do, of deed small or great, hidden or apparent. So know this, behave properly toward Allah, and think well of Him, and you will be saved from a destruction that is inevitable for one who thinks ill of Allah and behaves badly toward His Messenger, the Messenger of Allah."

Guidance from the verses:

1- A description of the nature of the people of the desert, which is harshness and coarseness and remoteness from courtesy and good manners.

2- An explanation of the difference between faith (iman) and Islam when they are combined: faith is the deeds of the heart and Islam is the deeds of the limbs. When they are separated, faith is Islam and Islam is faith. The reality is that there is no sound faith without sound Islam, and no sound Islam without sound faith; but there is a formal Islam without faith, and there is a false claim of faith that is not sincere.

3- A description of the believers in truth: those who believed in Allah and His Messenger, then did not doubt, and strove with their wealth and their lives.

4- An explanation of the ruling on al-mann (reminding of a favor): it is blameworthy from a human being and praiseworthy from the Most Merciful, the Mighty and Majestic. The reality of al-mann is counting a favor and mentioning it to the one who received it, enumerating it again and again.

5- An explanation of the comprehensiveness of Allah's knowledge of all creatures, and that nothing of the deeds of the servants is hidden from Him.
